content: === Introduction ===
An ectopia (/ɛkˈtoʊpiə/) is a displacement or malposition of an organ or other body part, which is then referred to as ectopic (/ɛkˈtɒpɪk/).[1]
=== Examples ===
<info> Ectopic ACTH syndrome, also known as small-cell carcinoma.
<info> Ectopic calcification, a pathologic deposition of calcium salts in tissues or bone growth in soft tissues
<info> Cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, aka Chiari malformation, a herniation of the brain through the foramen magnum, which may be congenital or caused by trauma.
<info> Ectopic cilia, a hair growing where it isn't supposed to be, commonly an eyelash on an abnormal spot on the eyelid, distichia
<info> Ectopia cordis, the displacement of the heart outside the body during fetal development
<info> Ectopic enamel, a tooth abnormality, where enamel is found in an unusual location, such as at the root of a tooth
<info> Ectopic expression, the expression of a gene in an abnormal place in an organism
<info> Ectopic hormone, a hormone produced by a tumor, such as small-cell carcinoma, can cause Cushing's syndrome
<info> Ectopia lentis, the displacement of the crystalline lens of the eye
<info> Ectopic pancreas, displacement of pancreatic tissue in the body with no connection, anatomical or vascular, to the pancreas
<info> Ectopic recombination, the recombination between sequences (like leu2 sequences) present at different genomic locations
<info> Renal ectopia occurs when both kidneys are on the same side of the body
<info> Ectopic testis, a testis that has moved to an unusual location
<info> Ectopic thymus,  where thymus tissue is found in an abnormal location
<info> Ectopic thyroid, where an entire or parts of the thyroid are located elsewhere in the body
<info> Ectopic tooth, a tooth that erupted outside the dental arch
<info> Ectopic ureter, where the ureter terminates somewhere other than the urinary bladder
<info> Ectopia vesicae,  a congenital anomaly in which part of the urinary bladder is present outside the body
=== See also ===
